content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies a wide range of factors that could affect adversarial robustness from an architectural perspective (mainly ResNet). In extensive empirical experiments, this paper identified that pre-activation and bottleneck block could greatly impact the robustness. This paper also shows adding a skip connection to Squeeze and Extraction (SE), and aggregated convolution is beneficial to the robustness. Finally, through a fine-grained search on depth, width, and scaling ratio, this paper proposes a RobustResNet architecture.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength 
- The extensive empirical evaluations are very comprehensive that include most elements of neural network architecture. Motivations for each component designing the Robust Residual Block is well explained.
- Proposed RobustResNet empirically demonstrated the effectiveness of a commonly used benchmark (AutoAttack).
- The overall presentation is easy to follow.

Weaknesses
- It's unclear why the observation of smoothed activation function is not consistent with existing works. This part of section 3.1.3 is unclear to me. What is the main message here? 
- I don't think upsampling from $32\times32$ images to higher resolution makes sense for studying kernel size in section 3.1.2. Upsample could lose information in the input. Perhaps cropping from a higher resolution would produce different results. 
- It would be nice to include the activation order in Table 1. It seems like the pre-act itself can significantly improve the robustness already (Figure 3 (b)). 
- All experiments are conducted with TRADES. It is unclear if other training strategies/methods could improve by using RobustResNet, see [RobustBench](https://robustbench.github.io) for other different methods. 
- All of the experiments are based on CIFAR-10 and some on Tiny-ImageNet. The entire paper and its contribution are empirically using single architecture. The results might not be generic on other datasets or architectures.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: very clear

Quality: good 

Novelty: limited

Reproducibility: open-source code is available in the supplementary materials.
content.summary_of_the_review: The comprehensive empirical observation/evaluations of different elements in the ResNet that could affect the adversarial robustness is the main merit of this paper. However, the lack of theoretical analysis and only focus on an architecture with a small-scale dataset might limit its contribution.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors study the effect of different architectural components in ResNets towards their adversarial robustness. Their experimental study leads them to propose Robust ResBlock. This increases $\ell_\infty$ - robustness across CIFAR-10/100, and TinyImageNet datasets across different adversarial attacks over existing architecture component based robust architectures at varying levels of parameters and FLOPS.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

The evaluation is very extensive. The array of models tested is large. The experiments and discussion on compound scaling is good and interesting. The improvements shown over other existing methods for architecture based robustness improvement are good.  The paper is well organized. 

Weakness:

Standard deviations are not shown everywhere which makes some of the conclusions drawn by authors unreliable, detailed below.

- In A.4, figure 13 (g) - pre-SE at r=16 has slightly lower params than the proposed SE and has better clean performance, the difference in robustness is marginal. One could also argue that there is no difference in robustness if the pre-SE model were to have more params (perhaps slightly larger dimensions in SE). Standard deviations in this setting hence become imperative, which were not shown. Hence, the conclusions drawn here seem a stretch.

- The argument w.r.t kernel size seems inconsistent  - there is clearly (albeit small) increase in rob.acc in fig 6 (e) at resolutions 64, 128 from kernel-size = 3 -> 5. Also trivially upscaling the images can lead to loss of coherence in cifar-like (low resolution) data - this could affect clean accuracy as well (numbers not shown).
I am not sure if this set of experiments is grounded enough to draw the conclusions drawn. So a statement like “kernel size of 3x3 remains the preferred choice” is not justified.

- In section 3.1.3 - activation,  the experiments are thorough as they take into account different parameters. But Gowal et al., also came to the same conclusion that relu might be enough. Quoting from Gowal et al. “However, in contrast to Xie et al., we found that other “smooth” activation functions do not necessarily improve robustness” and “Overall, ReLU remains a good choice”. This section and contained experiments seem unnecessary.

- LayerNorm does not converge -  maybe the TRADES setting used is very strict - I would suggest trying standard AT or a low Divergence term coefficient in TRADES here. Again standard deviations are missing in A.6 to draw a conclusive inference about BN, GN etc. This section adds to the inconsistencies in the paper.

- In Section 3.2.1, the ratios obtained are similar to Huang et al. who showed a 10:10:4 setting works best and this can be scaled for \alpha in {0.25, 0.5, 1.0,1.5, 2.0}. This should be highlighted - as there is not much novelty here.


References

Huang H, Wang Y, Erfani S, Gu Q, Bailey J, Ma X. Exploring architectural ingredients of adversarially robust deep neural networks. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems. 2021 Dec 6;34:5545-59.

Gowal S, Qin C, Uesato J, Mann T, Kohli P. Uncovering the limits of adversarial training against norm-bounded adversarial examples. arXiv preprint arXiv:2010.03593. 2020 Oct 7.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well written, has a lot of experiments but lacks novelty. The code is available and the results seem to be reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Overall, I think the paper studies an important often understudied aspect of robustness. I credit the authors for an extensive search of different aspects of architectural design. 

But, the authors could have focused more on the compound scaling (the main highlight of this work) result they have and conducted a more systematic ablation over how different changes in the proposed RobustResBlock aid in the overall gain in robustness. 
A complete restructuring of the paper to highlight the novelty of this work (compound scaling and Robust ResBlock) would make this paper better.

As it stands, it just seems inconsistent at times - kernel size argument, SE block conclusions, and not novel enough - Independent scaling of width and depth has already been studied by Huang et al., and findings of the activation section are similar to the conclusions drawn in Gowal et al and all other experiments/sections are only marginally novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper does a thorough empirical investigation of the effect of network architecture on the (empirical) robust accuracy of the trained network. The result is a portfolio of adversarially robust residual networks with a wide spectrum of model capacities that outperform standard networks under the same training conditions.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper does a thorough investigation of the relationship between network architecture and robust accuracy and does a good job of providing the information required for practitioners to understand and replicate the results.

However, the paper has three key weaknesses:

1. First, the robust networks created do not improve upon the state of the art (even when excluding methods that used additional data / synthetic images). For example, referencing the RobustBench leaderboard (https://robustbench.github.io/): "Towards Achieving Adversarial Robustness Beyond Perceptual Limits" achieves 58.04\% AutoAttack robust accuracy with a WRN-34-10. It is critical for the work to address this performance gap. (For example, the work could combine the architectural improvement found here with the other improvements from leading techniques). 
2. Second, the paper's approach does not provide incontrovertible evidence of the observed trends. In particular, it's possible that the trends observed (e.g. "pre-activation is preferred over post-activation for adversarial robustness") only hold for the particular slice of hyperparameters: when investigating activations, one has to fix the other aspects of the network, such as the activation function, kernel size, or relative depth/width of the network. I do recognize that given the combinatorial explosion in the number of networks for every possible combination of hyperparameters, it's not _really_ possible to show that a trend is true over every slice --- this is a fundamental limitation of the selected problem of searching a high-dimensional hyperparameter space.
3. Now, it's possible that the paper could be contributing by describing a useful search _approach_ that produces a good set of hyperparameters. In such a case, an important baseline to consider is neural architecture search (NAS) [1] with the same budget (either in compute time or the number of trained networks). A (conceptually) simple implementation would be to use a strong black-box optimizer like Open Source Vizier [2]. Demonstrating that RobustResNets consistently outperform a NAS baseline would make it clear that the approach of studying one parameter at a time is reasonable.

Concerns of less significance can be found in the section below.

[1]: Elsken, Thomas, Jan Hendrik Metzen, and Frank Hutter. "Neural architecture search: A survey." The Journal of Machine Learning Research 20.1 (2019): 1997-2017.
[2]: Song, Xingyou, et al. "Open Source Vizier: Distributed Infrastructure and API for Reliable and Flexible Blackbox Optimization." First Conference on Automated Machine Learning (Main Track). 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
### Clarity

The paper clearly describes what hyperparameters are being tuned and does a good job of summarizing the results in figures.

Unfortunately, the density of information sometimes detracts from clarity (e.g. removing PGD attacks from Figures 3 and 4, and possibly using slightly different hues could help make it easier to understand what's going on.). Additionally, likely in an effort to save space, the figures in the paper are small enough to make reading and comparison quite challenging.

Some additional concerns:

- Figures 8b-8d and 8f-8h are confusing to me. Are we showing an average of the best/worst performing networks at each depth? Are we simply showing a single network? A different view of this information might be helpful.
- Figure 3a shows a shaded blue region for one curve that is not present for any of the other curves. What does the shaded area correspond to?

### Quality
Some concerns in addition to those highlighted in the strengths & weaknesses section above:

- The evaluation metrics on Page 2 include FGSM, PGD, CW and AA, but results for the paper primarily focus on CW. (1. FGSM: Could not find in main body, but I would be fine excluding this since it is a weak attack; 2. PGD: Figure 3, 4 and Table 2; 3. AA: Only Table 2.) The comparison would be simplified if we just used the strongest attack (either AA, or a combination of the four methods outlined). Otherwise, the work should be clear that we are focusing only on CW [3].
- We need more evidence that the optimal value of $r_D$ for compound scaling is 0.7. Figure 9 clearly demonstrates that compound scaling outperforms standard scaling, but shows no results for $r_D \ge 0.8$. (Also, no details are provided about the function family from which the curves are selected or what the shaded area correspond to).

[3] A valid reason to do this might be that AA is simply too costly, or that rank order under CW and AA is assumed to be similar.

### Novelty
To the best of my knowledge, this is the first large-scale study of the impact of changing all architectural components.

In addition to the empirical exploration of the effect of network parameters, the work also introduces a novel modification to the existing "squeeze-and-excitation" module that works better for robust training.

### Reproducibility

The amount of detail provided means that the paper is reproducible (although the large amount of compute required might mean that it is only possible to reproduce the entire paper in a larger lab.)
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper provides a thorough investigation of various network hyperparameters, resulting in networks which improve on the Pareto frontier of robust accuracy. The approach does not provide incontrovertible evidence of the claimed trends, and an important baseline is missing. Most importantly, the networks trained do not perform better than comparable techniques: https://robustbench.github.io/#leaderboard, making it hard to understand whether the architectural improvements found are of real value. Nevertheless, I am open to being convinced by other reviewers that the architecture improvements found here would be of value to the community.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies the relation between adversarial robustness and deep network architecture. It separately investigate two different angles: network block design (model topology) and network scaling factor (model complexity). With experiments on many benchmarks and models, the authors summarize 6 major observations and create a robust model under constrained amount of complexity.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strength
1. The studied topic is important and meaningful. Concurrent research directions such as adversarial training seem to have entered a bottleneck period. It is urgent and very necessary to explore intrinsically robust deep architectures for further improvement of robustness. 
2. The empirical results in this work seems sound enough to me and can help practitioners in real life.
3. Some findings in this paper align with my experience in adversarial training. For instance, I also find the influence of smooth activation is not very obvious in practice.

## Weakness 
1. The biggest problem of this paper is that the content of the paper is mostly empirical observations. The authors did not provide insights or understandings on these observations they find. Claim such as "Pre-activation is preferred over post-activation for adversarial robustness." and "Squeeze and excitation with minor customization improves adversarial robustness." are not very interesting. For instance, if the observations are flipped: "Post-activation is preferred over pre-activation for adversarial robustness." and "Squeeze and excitation with minor customization does not improve adversarial robustness.", the current understandings of adversarial robustness is still not increased. We still do not understand why it improves or not improves robustness. Such examples are not alone. All the six observations have this problem. 
2. As an empirical work, this paper has done a lot of experiments. However, to support their claim, the experiments are comprehensive enough. For instance, there are tens of activation functions, most of which only have little difference. The authors only test 4 of them and claim ReLU would be the better choice under weight decay, which is not very convincing. Also, the results in table2, as one of the major contribution of this work, is not the sota results. Currently methods can easily reach 60\% robust accuracy against AA. The scores in the table is relatively low.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is clearly written and easy to follow. The quality is fair enough. The novelty is not so much.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper conducts very comprehensive empirical study about architecture design, block topology, and network scaling to reach a conclusion about the combination that enhances adversarial robustness.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The paper is well-written and well-presented.
- The experiments conducted are very comprehensive.  
- The empirical observations are useful to the community. 

Weaknesses
- Although the observations are useful, the paper is less innovative. It mainly tries existed components to see if they can improve adversarial robustness.
- Images in figure 2 are blurry when zooming in.
- It lacks of visualizations and explanations regarding why the preferred choices of residual block, the order of activation, activation, and so on are better than others. I believe these insights are more important than just saying these choices are better.
- Even for the ideal architecture, the obtained robust accuracies are significantly lower than the reported SOTA in RobustBench. I understand the purpose is not to gain SOTA performances. However, it would be more convincing if the preferred choices when plugging into a SOTA model can help to improve it. Otherwise, these findings cannot be generalized to other works.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-written and well-presented. The empirical findings and observations are interesting through very comprehensive experiments. However, the paper is less innovative.  It mainly tries existed components to see if they can improve adversarial robustness.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is well-written and well-presented. Very comprehensive experiments were conducted to reach useful empirical findings and observations for improving adversarial robustness. However, the paper is less innovative. It also lacks of visualizations and explanations regarding why the preferred choices of residual block, the order of activation, activation, and so on are better than others. It would be great of the authors can demonstrate an improvement to an existing SOTA approach so that we can believe the findings can be generalized to other works.
